title: Sky Sentinel, an AI-controlled machine-gun turret built by Ukrainian engineers, is reported to have downed four Shahed drones with one prototype; UNITED24 raises $1.5 million for 10 units
summary: Ukraine's Sky Sentinel, an AI-controlled heavy-machine-gun turret, is reported to have downed four Russian Shahed drones with one prototype; dates and places are withheld (May-June 2025).
account: Sky Sentinel is an autonomous turret, a heavy machine gun on a 360-degree mount whose software, written by Ukrainian engineers, takes radar input, separates drones from birds, tracks the target, computes the ballistic solution and fires without a human; UNITED24 Media, the outlet of the UNITED24 fundraising platform, reported on May 26, 2025 that one prototype had downed four Shahed drones at the front, with dates and places withheld for security, and that its $1.5 million campaign for 10 turrets at about $150,000 each was complete. Forbes (David Hambling, May 27, 2025), as relayed by Euromaidan Press on May 28, 2025, repeats the four kills and gives a pointing precision of 17 micro-radians, and The Defense Post (June 3, 2025) adds that 10 to 30 units would be needed to protect a city and that production is scaling to dozens a month. The Monitor's statement that a human authorizes each shot is not in any fetched report.
purpose: Built to shoot down Shahed-type attack drones and other small air targets automatically; the reported interceptions are that purpose.
system: Sky Sentinel AI-controlled anti-drone turret (heavy machine gun, radar-cued)
developer: Ukrainian engineering team (not named in the reports)
taxonomy_note: Trustible has no military-defense type; the reported good is attack drones destroyed before reaching their targets, counted here as weapons removed, the nearest fit to Reduced Violence.

ratings.reason: Four shoot-downs are reported by the fundraising platform with no dates, places or targets, so no protected population or averted strike is documented.
The reports do not identify the unit that fielded the prototype or any result beyond the kill count.

ai_role.statement: Per UNITED24 Media and Forbes via Euromaidan Press, the AI does the whole engagement: it takes radar data, distinguishes drones from birds, tracks the flight path, computes the shot with wind and target speed, and fires conventional rounds. The four kills are the makers' claim relayed by the fundraiser; no independent confirmation, footage date or location is given, and the Monitor's human-authorization step does not appear in the fetched reports.

produced_by: Radar cueing that hands the turret a track on a slow, low-flying drone
A fixed heavy-machine-gun mount with near-zero mechanical play and fast optics
Rules that let the system engage without a human in the loop
must_hold: Targets fly within the gun's effective range and are not masked by birds or clutter
Enough units are fielded to cover a city, which the makers put at 10 to 30

claim_basis: Two independent news reports, a registry entry and the deployer's news report are on file. There is no independent study or report and no finding by a regulator or court.
